headline: High risk: Replit Agent can write broad workspace state while dbt-core can touch warehouse data, creating dangerous data-handling and workflow-conflict pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No direct shared channel is documented between dbt-core and Replit Agent, so prompt injection is not default. However, Replit Agent can read/write Repl workspace files and dbt-core operates on data warehouse data, so a manual file bridge could carry malicious instructions. The pathway is unusual and the blast radius is limited.
conditions: IF the operator copies dbt-generated text into Replit workspace files or prompts
IF Replit Agent is instructed to parse dbt output as instructions
mitigations: Keep dbt artifacts out of the Replit workspace
Use a strict prompt template that ignores file contents as instructions
Review copied text before pasting into Replit
Store instructions in a separate, read-only note
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to imported files

B_data_leakage.rationale: dbt-core touches data warehouse data and Replit Agent touches source code, secrets, and deployment configuration while having broad network egress. Replit Agent also reads workspace files by default, so if warehouse outputs or secrets are placed in the shared workspace, sensitive data can flow into a third-party-backed agent. This is plausible in default workflows, though not proven by direct pair evidence.
conditions: IF warehouse extracts or secrets are written into the Repl workspace
IF Replit Agent is asked to inspect or transform those files
mitigations: Do not place warehouse exports in the Repl workspace
Redact secrets before any file handoff
Restrict Replit Agent to synthetic sample data
Audit outbound network destinations before running
requires-engineering: segregate sensitive data into a separate environment

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Replit Agent has write_filesystem, modify_git_state, execute_shell, and broad network egress, while dbt-core calls data warehouse APIs and handles data warehouse data. If both operate on the same project or deployment artifacts, concurrent edits and state changes can corrupt git state or pipeline outputs. The profiles show overlapping mutable surfaces and no locking mechanism, so uncertainty pushes this to high.
conditions: IF both agents modify the same repo or workspace
IF dbt runs while Replit Agent edits models, configs, or git state
mitigations: Pause one agent before the other edits shared files
Use separate branches for dbt and Replit changes
Commit frequently to reduce merge conflicts
Lock the workspace during dbt runs
requires-engineering: add orchestration-level file locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: dbt-core can generate transformed data and artifacts that Replit Agent may then read from workspace files or use in coding tasks. Replit Agent is capable of acting on files and shell commands, so if it treats dbt output as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into code or deployment changes. The interaction is plausible but not directly documented, so medium fits.
conditions: IF Replit Agent consumes dbt outputs as ground truth
IF downstream shell or file edits are made without validation
mitigations: Require a human review step between dbt and Replit actions
Validate dbt outputs against source data checks
Use read-only exports for handoff
Ask Replit Agent to summarize, not execute, dbt findings
requires-engineering: add automated schema and data-quality gates

E_compliance.rationale: dbt-core touches data warehouse data, while Replit Agent handles secrets and deployment configuration in a cloud Repl environment with broad network egress. That creates a plausible residency and retention mismatch if regulated data is moved into Replit-managed storage or logs. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction breach, so medium is appropriate rather than high.
conditions: IF regulated warehouse data is copied into Replit-managed files or logs
IF the data subject to retention rules is processed by both agents
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Replit workspaces
Use masked or synthetic datasets
Check retention settings before uploading files
Document the data flow for compliance review
requires-engineering: enforce residency controls and DPA review
